lines.text: What would happen to the United States if a catastrophic event knocked out the power grid nationwide?
Within seconds, three hundred and thirty million Americans would plunge into pitch black silence.
Refrigeration fails instantly, spoiling millions of tons of food in grocery distribution warehouses.
Within twenty-four hours, municipal water pumping stations lose backup diesel, running taps dry.
Hospitals burn through emergency generator fuel while cell phone towers die one by one.
Because massive custom high-voltage transformers take months to manufacture, recovery would take years.
The electrical grid is the fragile heartbeat sustaining all modern American life.
